[image caption · medium · regular] (Image of a silver car)

[disclosure · medium · bold red] Representative APR: 209.8%

claims.claim: If you’re looking for a fast and reliable logbook lender... you can stop looking! (speed/ease incentive) accompanied within the same image by Representative APR: 209.8%
claims.rationale: 'Fast and reliable logbook lender' is a statement about the speed and quality of service - an incentive to apply for credit under CONC 3.5.7R(1)(c) as glossed by CONC 3.5.8G(4) - and the same image displays 'Representative APR: 209.8%' in [medium · bold red], so the representative APR the trigger requires is present within the standalone communication, the structure FG15/4 endorses for inserted images. Scoped to the representative APR's presence; its relative prominence (CONC 3.5.7R(2)) is not addressed by FG15/4 (see notes).

label_authority.source: FCA FG15/4: Social media and customer communications (March 2015)
label_authority.quote: In the Guidance Consultation, we explained that if firms cannot ensure that the image (such as an infographic) will always be displayed automatically (users may switch off images to save on data usage) then both the invitation/inducement and the risk warning/balancing statement would need to be provided within the inserted image.
label_authority.rule_cited_by_source: CONC 3 (FG15/4 fn 5, ¶1.15) - no pinpoint; CONC 3.5.7R/3.5.8G(4) are the operative representative-APR provisions, drift-checked against the current corpus

claims.claim: Click here for our latest promotion (signposting tweet text carrying no rate of interest or cost-of-credit figure; the only cost figure in the whole promotion is the representative APR inside the image)
claims.rationale: The tweet text outside the image ('Click here for our latest promotion') contains no rate of interest and no amount relating to the cost of credit, so it carries no CONC 3.5.3R(1) trigger - exactly the no-'trigger'-information signposting FG15/4 prescribes; inside the image the only cost figure is the representative APR itself, and CONC 3.5.3R(2) disapplies the representative-example requirement for a promotion falling within CONC 3.5.7R that indicates no rate or cost figure other than the representative APR. Scoped to the representative-example limb (CONC 3.5.3R(1)(a) via (2)); the postal-address limb (1)(b) is a separate, un-carried question (see notes).

label_authority.source: FCA FG15/4: Social media and customer communications (March 2015)
label_authority.quote: Firms may wish to ensure therefore that the initial tweet or post does not contain any ‘trigger’ information but merely links through to a webpage where all the information is shown together.
label_authority.rule_cited_by_source: representative-example trigger for consumer credit (FG15/4 p9 signposting examples; Annex ¶2.2) - CONC 3.5.3R not pinpointed by the source, drift-checked against the current corpus

claims.claim: The image indicates a rate (RAPR 209.8%) but no postal address is visible; CONC 3.5.3R(1)(b) requires the firm’s postal address when a promotion includes a rate — whether the surrounding post carried it cannot be determined from the inserted-image fragment
claims.rationale: A rate is indicated ('Representative APR: 209.8%'), so CONC 3.5.3R(1) is engaged and (1)(b) requires a postal address at which the person making the promotion may be contacted; (2) disapplies only the (1)(a) representative-example limb, and none of the (3) exceptions (television/radio broadcast, dealer or lender premises, dealer name-and-address, credit-broker name-and-postal-address) is engaged by the visible content. No postal address appears anywhere in the transcription, but the annotated inserted-image fragment cannot establish whether the complete promotion as displayed carried one, so the determination needs a human.

label_authority.quote: (1) Where a financial promotion indicates a rate of interest or an amount relating to the cost of credit whether expressed as a sum of money or a proportion of a specified amount, the financial promotion must also: (a) include a representative example in accordance with CONC 3.5.5 R, and (b) specify a postal address at which the person making the financial promotion may be contacted.

notes: VERDICT IS INFERRED, not FCA-stated: FG15/4 presents Fig 6 as an exemplar without a verdict label (its caption is just 'Consumer Credit inserted images example'); the compliant labels rest on the annotated content mechanically satisfying current CONC 3.5.7R/3.5.8G(4)/3.5.3R(2) - owner must ratify this inference at sign-off. The only consumer-credit image in FG15/4 and the only corpus-mappable example. Drift check (2015 -> current corpus text): CONC 3.5.7R still carries the representative-APR triggers at (1)(a)-(c) - post-2020 additions (1A) and (3) (payment-account carve-out; overdraft/0%-APR/community-finance exclusions) do not touch this promotion; CONC 3.5.8G(4) still glosses speed/ease statements as incentives; CONC 3.5.3R still carries the representative-example trigger and its (2) exemption for representative-APR-only promotions within 3.5.7R (post-2015 addition (2A), 0%-APR agreements, not relevant). Logbook (bill-of-sale) credit is excluded from the HCSTC definition, so no CONC 3.4.1R warning arises. The CONC 3.5.3R(1)(b) postal-address question is carried as claim 3 under Handbook authority per owner ruling; still NOT carried (no FG15/4 authority; left un-carried at sign-off): CONC 3.5.7R(2) relative prominence of the representative APR; CONC 3.5.9R APR formatting. CP26/15 (2026) is consulting on CONC 3 changes; labels as-verified at authoring date. Owner ruling 2026-08-09: (1)(b) carried as needs_review - fragment cannot determine; inferred-compliant verdicts on claims 1-2 ratified.
